title: Shanghai's Pudong Was Farmland in 1990 — Now a 632m Skyline | China Travel Expert
description:
Stand on the Bund today and the wall of towers across the river looks like it has always been there. It hasn't. In 1990, Shanghai's Pudong — the east bank — was mostly farmland and warehouses.

That April, China opened Pudong for development, and Lujiazui went up on the fields. Today it's one of the densest clusters of supertall towers on Earth, topped by the Shanghai Tower at 632 metres — China's tallest building and the second-tallest in the world. Barely thirty years from paddies to a forest of skyscrapers.

🧭 Expert Tip: for the best view, stand on the Bund across the Huangpu River — the whole Pudong skyline lines up in one frame, and it's free.

1990年浦东大多还是农田；那年四月开放开发，陆家嘴拔地而起。如今最高的上海中心632米——中国第一高。三十年，从农田到超高层森林。
